R5C-bear-backcountry-0002.name: By Chilcotin River
R5C-bear-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R5C-bear-backcountry-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2018 (8 years old), 110 m E: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2017 (fire C10784), 120 m SW: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 12 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Chilcotin River 50 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Chilanko Forks, about 62 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Puntzi Airport Rd, Puntzi Mountain Rd, Puntzi Lake FSR, 4118-6A,13,15A,17A.
Park: 52.47995, -124.4244, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 8.3 km N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 345 m, about 201 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 280 m NW of the spot at 1,220 m (52.55661, -124.42834). Water: Chilcotin River 70 m NW (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-12, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-15, closures 2026-10-16.
R5C-bear-backcountry-0002.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-12: about 412 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.04 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
